Objective
---------
Fix the parser, the docs patch, and the curation rules; regenerate
all committed outputs; verify the compose vendor; integrate the
DOCS_PORT delta. Deliverables (updated in place, outputs regenerated):

  scripts/dev/parse-labs.py      v2
  scripts/dev/patch-docs.py      v2

Bump a version header comment in each .py file and summarise the
change in one line.

Task 1 — parse-labs.py v2
-------------------------
a. CWD SIMULATION: within each lab file, process commands in order.
   `cd X` updates the simulated cwd (relative to the track repo root;
   handle `..` and absolute paths). Every subsequent build/run
   command resolves its context (and -f path) against the CURRENT
   simulated cwd, not the repo root. Record "cwd" per command in the
   JSON. This alone should collapse the doubled contexts
   (…v0.5/…v0.5 -> …v0.5) and make `.` contexts meaningful.
b. PLACEHOLDER RESOLUTION: after cwd resolution, if a context still
   contains a placeholder token ([VERSION], {VERSION}, -VERSION,
   _VERSION, or a literal all-caps segment), glob the track repo for
   directories matching the literal prefix/suffix pattern around the
   token (e.g. intro-to-instrument-*). Exactly one match ->
   substitute and record the decision in "assumptions". Multiple
   matches -> choose the highest version (semver-aware), record the
   choice AND the alternatives in parse-warnings.txt. No match ->
   check whether an EARLIER command in the same lab (or an earlier
   lab, same track) creates the directory (wget/curl -O, git clone,
   unzip, tar, cp); if so, mark the build runtime_download=true and
   write the source URL(s) to content/extracted/runtime-downloads.txt
   with the lab filename; if no creator exists anywhere, mark
   interactive_context=true as before.
c. DEDUPE: identical (file, raw) command occurrences collapse to one
   entry with "occurrences": N. Different raws building the SAME tag
   are NOT deduped, but every duplicate tag across a track is listed
   in parse-warnings.txt (the preload executor skips already-built
   tags).
d. FLAG DETECTION: detect docker-buildx-only flags on build/run
   commands — --load, --push, --builder, --provenance, --sbom —
   recording them in syntax_flags with the specific flag name.
   (--platform is supported by buildah; do NOT flag it.) These
   commands are NOT skipped at preload; the executor strips the
   unsupported flags. Record stripping as a documented
   transformation.
e. EXHAUSTIVE FROM EXTRACTION: beyond build-context Dockerfiles and
   build-command-embedded Dockerfiles, scan ALL code blocks in ALL
   lab files (any path variant) for Dockerfile-looking content
   (FROM/AS lines in fenced blocks, with or without an associated
   build command) and merge every FROM reference into
   external-images.txt. Rationale: attendee-created Dockerfiles
   (interactive labs) only exist as HTML content; their FROM bases
   must still be preloaded or the attendee's build fails offline.
f. PULL RE-CHECK: after v2 parsing, report whether ANY docker/podman
   pull commands exist across all lab files. If they exist in
   content/repos HTML, the docs patch (Task 2) must cover the repo
   copies too. If genuinely none exist, say so explicitly — podman
   auto-pulls on `run`, which the preload makes a no-op.
g. Re-emit all outputs: commands.json (now with cwd, occurrences,
   assumptions, flags), external-images.txt (merged FROMs),
   build-failures-expected.txt (expect MUCH shorter — only
   interactive_context or unresolvable contexts), syntax-risk.txt
   (now flag-level detail), runtime-downloads.txt (may be empty),
   parse-warnings.txt.
Print: per-track unique build tags, unique run commands, pulls,
externals added this pass, the placeholder resolution table
(placeholder -> resolved directory), and the expected-skip count
delta (was 36).

Task 2 — patch-docs.py v2
-------------------------
a. Patch BOTH content/docs/<track>/**.html AND
   content/repos/<track>/lab*.html (+ index/landing pages) —
   attendees may open either copy.
b. Keep the existing banner + PRELOADED pull-marker rules (harmless
   if no pulls exist).
c. NEW RULE: rewrite `docker build --load` -> `docker build` inside
   code blocks in BOTH trees, appending the note
   "# --load removed: buildx-only flag; podman loads by default".
   Log per-track rewrite counts to docs-patched.txt.
d. Idempotent: re-running must not double-apply (banner insertion
   and marker appends must detect prior application).

Task 3 — check-docs.py (NEW)
----------------------------
For every track: crawl content/docs/<track>/**.html (and repo lab
HTML), extract every src= and href= reference, and verify the target
exists on local disk (relative to the page). Report per track: pages
checked, references checked, MISSING list with the referencing page.
For otel-developers specifically (the mirror reported an upstream
subresource error): retry the mirror for missing assets once
(targeted wget of the missing paths), then re-verify. Whatever
remains missing goes to content/extracted/docs-gaps.txt with
referencing pages. Non-fatal, but the report must be explicit —
broken attendee docs are a day-of problem.

Task 4 — curate.py v2
---------------------
Replace the selection rule. New rules:
a. Selection is across ALL lab files and path variants for the
   track; engine is NOT a filter (the VM executes everything via the
   podman-docker shim -> rootful podman; both engines share one
   image store). Each entry records "exec": "docker" and keeps
   source.engine + source.raw as evidence.
b. Per track, curate the PRIMARY service-start commands:
     opentelemetry:   find the Jaeger run command in ANY lab file
                      (all variants). Expect check
                      http://localhost:16686 contains "Jaeger".
     otel-developers: keep the existing Jaeger entry (lab03) —
                      re-validate against cwd-corrected parsing.
     prometheus:      keep workshop-prometheus:v3.13 run (lab05),
                      check :9090/-/ready contains "Prometheus";
                      ALSO curate prometheus_services_demo:v1 from
                      lab03/lab07 (context installs/demo — now
                      resolvable) with its exact ports/env from the
                      lab command.
     fluentbit:       find the fluent-bit run command(s) that
                      publish a host port (any variant; the 2020
                      HTTP-metrics port is the candidate but ONLY
                      if a lab command actually publishes it —
                      quote the command). Curate with exact volume
                      mounts; if a mounted config file is
                      attendee-created in the lab, record that as a
                      "verify-time prep" step (generate the file
                      from the lab HTML content before running) —
                      do not invent the mount. If NO lab command
                      publishes any host port for fluent-bit,
                      curate the container-start command with a
                      running-check (see c) and say so.
     perses:          curate the Perses run from the suffixed path
                      where it lives, check http://localhost:8080
                      (docs establish 8080 — docs win) expecting
                      "Perses"; ALSO curate node-exporter from
                      lab05-podman.html, check :9100/metrics
                      contains "node_".
c. Check fallback: for SPA frontends (Perses, Jaeger UI), confirm the
   expect substring against the mirrored docs' HTML or the page
   <title> — the literal string may only appear there, not in the
   app shell. If the substring cannot be confirmed anywhere, use
   {"type": "running"} — container must be Up — and record why.
   Running-checks are a weaker but honest signal.
d. EXEC ADAPTATIONS: every entry gets "exec_adaptations": [ ... ]
   documenting every deviation from the raw command, e.g.
   "-it stripped (no TTY in verification)", "detached (-d added)",
   "--load stripped (buildx-only)". No undocumented deviations.
e. Regenerate curated.json; keep "unresolved" for anything still not
   curable, but each unresolved entry must now state precisely which
   files were searched and what WAS found (quote or near-quote).

lab-vm.conf was generated by prompt 10r and predates the port

  - add ONE variable with a comment:
      DOCS_PORT="8090"   # the in-VM docs server; Perses publishes

                         # so the docs server must not use 8080.
                         # Consumed by script 70 (prompt 11r).

change references to Perses' own 8080. If no references exist yet,
record at the bottom of lab-vm.conf: "# 11r: docs server + START-HERE
must use $DOCS_PORT, never 8080 (Perses owns 8080)".

Task 6 — compose vendored-binary verification (NEW)
---------------------------------------------------
The 10s feedback records "Compose v5.6.0 is vendored". The docker
compose CLI release line is v2.x — there is no v5.6.0 docker-compose.
Verify, and paste evidence:
  - run content/bin/docker-compose-v2 --version on this machine;
    paste the exact output
  - confirm the source URL recorded in versions.lock is an official
    docker compose release artifact (github.com/docker/compose
    releases)
  - confirm content/bin/docker-compose-v2.sha256 matches the binary
If the version string does NOT parse as v2.y.z, or the source URL is
not an official release, or the binary is not docker compose at all:
  re-vendor the latest stable v2.x linux x86_64 release from the
  official source, regenerate the sha256 file, update versions.lock
  (URL + version), and note the correction in
  content/extracted/parse-warnings.txt with the old and new versions.
Rationale: prompt 11r's 50-user-setup installs this binary as the
compose backend against podman.socket — a wrong binary is a latent
day-of failure. Compose is robustness only (zero lab usage), but the
artifact must be the real thing.

5. Per-track unique-tag counts vs the previous occurrence counts.
6. check-docs.py report summary per track, plus docs-gaps.txt if

9. Statement: everything ran online; no learner-vm provisioning
   script exists or was touched; the VM was not accessed.
